about: The chart benchmark: the 24 requests of fixtures/chart-benchmark.json, which ticket 25 measured the chart quality pass on, plus eight more, each with the statement we would have written for it and the rows that statement returns. `shape` is the shape the plan pass should choose and `also` lists the shapes that answer the same request just as honestly. `roles` is what the columns have to be, in order: a position or a label, an optional series, and the euro figure last. Ticket 38.
profile: fixtures/synthetic/sparkasse-2025.csv, imported through the Sparkasse preset and categorized by rules and the merchant dictionary only: 433 bookings, 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-28, 384 categorized and 49 Needs review.
scoring: shape match: the plan chose `shape` or one of `also`. columns map: the rows carry one column per role, in order, with the euro figure numeric and the names not. figure match: every number in the gold rows comes back in the chart's own rows, to the cent. first attempt: the self-check passed with no repair round. drawn: there is a chart, which is `rendered`.
checklist: shape: the drawing matches the comparison the request asks for
axis: the euro axis starts at zero for bars and areas; a line that does not is marked as truncated
labels: every category label is readable, thinned or rotated rather than dropped or overlapping
legend: present with more than one series, absent with one
colours: from the theme palette, in a stable order
language: the title is in the language of the request, and so are the month labels
money: euros formatted the German way on ticks and in the tooltip
junk: no title, no height, no second axis, no decoration inside the frame
tooltip: hovering a mark shows the category and the euro figure

prompts.prompt: Show me my total spending per month in 2025 as a line chart.
prompts.why: The plain twelve-point series. Every other line chart in the set is this one with a filter on it.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Wie haben sich meine Ausgaben pro Monat 2025 entwickelt? Zeig es als Liniendiagramm.
prompts.why: The same series asked for in German, so the caption and the month labels have to be German too.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Chart my cumulative spending over 2025 as an area chart.
prompts.why: A running total, which is a window function in the statement and an area that rests on zero in the drawing.
prompts.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Zeig die kumulierten Ausgaben 2025 als Flaechendiagramm.
prompts.why: The German running total. The last point is the year's total, which is the quick check that the frame is right.
prompts.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Show my spending per category in 2025 as a bar chart.
prompts.why: Eleven named bars, one of them the Needs review bucket. Every name has to be drawn, which is what thinning the labels breaks.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Ausgaben pro Kategorie 2025 als Balkendiagramm.
prompts.why: The same eleven bars in German. The category names stay English because they are the profile's own data.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Which merchants took the most money in 2025? Show the top ten as a horizontal bar chart.
prompts.why: A ranking with long merchant names, which is what the horizontal bars are for. The statement names merchants by their enriched title.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 10

prompts.prompt: Zeig die zehn groessten Haendler 2025 als liegendes Balkendiagramm.
prompts.why: The German ranking. Ten rows means ten labels down the side and none of them may be dropped.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 10

prompts.prompt: Compare what I spent on groceries and on dining per quarter in 2025 as grouped bars.
prompts.why: Two categories across four quarters: eight rows and one figure per pair, which is what a grouped bar needs.
prompts.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Dining') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

prompts.prompt: Vergleiche Lebensmittel und Restaurants pro Quartal 2025 als gruppierte Balken.
prompts.why: The German version. A chart captioned by quarter may not have months along its axis.
prompts.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Dining') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

prompts.prompt: Show my monthly spending split by category in 2025 as a stacked bar chart.
prompts.why: Twelve months by eleven categories, which is more groups than the palette has colours: the app keeps the five largest under their own names and sums the rest itself, so gold is those five and the statement must not fold anything.
prompts.sql: WITH largest AS (SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY SUM(amount) ASC LIMIT 5) SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (SELECT topic FROM largest) GROUP BY month, topic ORDER BY month, topic

prompts.prompt: Monatliche Ausgaben nach Kategorie 2025 als gestapelte Balken.
prompts.why: The German stack, and the same five groups. Asking the statement to relabel the small categories is what broke this chart three rounds running: it grouped by the month alone and every month came back carrying several Other rows.
prompts.sql: WITH largest AS (SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY SUM(amount) ASC LIMIT 5) SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (SELECT topic FROM largest) GROUP BY month, topic ORDER BY month, topic

prompts.prompt: Show the share of my 2025 spending by category as a doughnut.
prompts.why: More categories than a doughnut has slices. Gold is the five largest, because those five survive whether the query asks for six or the app folds eleven.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5

prompts.prompt: Zeig den Anteil der groessten Haendler an meinen Ausgaben 2025 als Donut.
prompts.why: The same fold over merchants, in German. Raw booking text is too long for a legend, so the merchant is its enriched title.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5

prompts.prompt: Draw a sankey of my 2025 income flowing into the spending categories.
prompts.why: A flow with one source and eleven targets. Every link needs both ends and a positive amount, and a total row would be a flow into itself.
prompts.sql: SELECT 'Income' AS source, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS target, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY target ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Zeig als Sankey, wie mein Einkommen 2025 in die Ausgabenkategorien fliesst.
prompts.why: The German flow. The one source is named in the request's language, which is the only string in the chart the data does not supply.
prompts.sql: SELECT 'Einkommen' AS source, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS target, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY target ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Compare my total spending in the first half of 2025 with the second half in a chart.
prompts.why: Two bars and nothing else. A line between two points would draw a trend through six months nobody asked about.
prompts.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN booked_on < '2025-07-01' THEN 'H1' ELSE 'H2' END AS half, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY half ORDER BY half

prompts.prompt: Vergleiche meine Ausgaben im Januar 2025 mit denen im Juli 2025 als Diagramm.
prompts.why: Two months that are not next to each other, so the period cannot be one BETWEEN. Two bars again.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-01-31' OR booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-07-31') GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Chart my spending per quarter in 2025.
prompts.why: No shape is named, so the plan pass has to pick one that reads. Four quarters are bars, and a line over four points is defensible too.
prompts.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter

prompts.prompt: Show my spending per day in March 2025 as a line chart.
prompts.why: Days, not months, so the axis labels carry the day and may be thinned. Nineteen ticks reading 2025-03 is the failure this one catches.
prompts.sql: SELECT booked_on AS day, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

prompts.prompt: Show what I spent on groceries per month in 2025.
prompts.why: A narrow range over twelve months, so the euro axis has to include zero or a fifth of a difference reads as a cliff.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Zeig die Ausgaben aller Kategorien 2025 als Balkendiagramm, auch die kleinen.
prompts.why: All eleven categories, small ones included, which is a crowded category axis and no place to drop a label.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Chart my income and my spending per month in 2025 side by side.
prompts.why: Two series out of one signed column, which is a UNION of two branches and never two euro columns in one row: two marks drawing two figures with nothing to tell them apart stack income on top of spending.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, 'Income' AS topic, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents > 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month UNION ALL SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, 'Spending' AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month, topic

prompts.prompt: Zeig den monatlichen Saldo 2025, also Einnahmen minus Ausgaben, als Diagramm.
prompts.why: The one chart whose figures can be negative, so the zero line is inside the plot and not under it.
prompts.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS net_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Zeig als Donut, wie sich meine Lebensmittelausgaben 2025 auf die einzelnen Maerkte verteilen.
prompts.why: Nine merchants inside one category and six slices, so five of them are named and the rest is one slice. Gold is the five largest, which survive the fold either way.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5

prompts.prompt: Draw a sankey of how my 2025 spending flows from its categories into their subcategories.
prompts.why: A flow whose two ends are both columns of the view. Rows without a subcategory have no target, and a link with one end missing refuses the whole graph.
prompts.sql: SELECT category AS source, subcategory AS target, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND category IS NOT NULL AND subcategory IS NOT NULL GROUP BY source, target ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Zeig mir als Diagramm, wie viel von meinen Ausgaben 2025 kategorisiert ist und wie viel noch in Needs review liegt.
prompts.why: Two bars out of a column that is NULL or not. Needs review is an absence, so the statement asks for `category IS NULL` and never for a category of that name.
prompts.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN category IS NULL THEN 'Needs review' ELSE 'Kategorisiert' END AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY topic

prompts.prompt: Wie verteilen sich meine PayPal-Zahlungen an Freunde 2025? Zeig es als Donut.
prompts.why: Four people behind one counterparty. Their names are only in the enriched title, so a doughnut grouped by the counterparty is one slice and answers nothing.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%paypal%' GROUP BY person ORDER BY total_eur DESC

prompts.prompt: Zeig meine taeglichen Ausgaben im Dezember 2025 als Liniendiagramm.
prompts.why: Days along the axis in German, so the labels are days and not the month twenty times, and the euro axis still has to include zero.
prompts.sql: SELECT booked_on AS day, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day

prompts.prompt: Show my grocery spending per quarter in 2025, split into supermarket, bakery and drugstore, as a stacked bar chart.
prompts.why: The series is a subcategory rather than a category, and the request names the three it wants. Twelve rows, one per quarter and series, and never two for the same pair.
prompts.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, subcategory AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

prompts.prompt: Zeig die kumulierten Lebensmittelausgaben 2025 als Flaechendiagramm.
prompts.why: A running total inside one category. The area rests on zero by itself, so its euro axis names no domain of its own.
prompts.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month

prompts.prompt: Which five merchants took the most money in the second half of 2025? Show them as horizontal bars.
prompts.why: A ranking inside a period that is neither a month nor the year, so the period and the LIMIT have to survive the same statement.
prompts.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5
